segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אַף הַנָּשִׁים שֶׁאֵינָן נֶאֱמָנוֹת לוֹמַר ״מֵת בַּעְלָהּ״, נֶאֱמָנוֹת לְהָבִיא אֶת גִּיטָּהּ – חֲמוֹתָהּ, וּבַת חֲמוֹתָהּ, וְצָרָתָהּ, וִיבִמְתָּהּ, וּבַת בַּעְלָהּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» There are instances in which a woman’s testimony that another woman’s husband has died is not deemed credible (Yevamot 117a). If there is a presumption that due to their familial relationship the two women hate each other, there is concern that the woman is testifying falsely in order to harm the other woman. By doing so, she can cause the other woman to remarry. If her original husband then proves to be living, she will be required to leave her second husband. This mishna teaches: «Even the women who are not deemed credible to» testify on behalf of a woman and «say: Her husband died,» and she is permitted to remarry, «are deemed credible to bring her bill of divorce.» The relatives of the woman who are not deemed credible to testify that her husband has died are: «Her mother-in-law; and her mother-in-law’s daughter; and her rival wife,» i.e., another wife of her husband’s; «and her yevama,» i.e., her husband’s brother’s wife; «and her husband’s daughter.»

segments.he: מָה בֵּין גֵּט לְמִיתָה? שֶׁהַכְּתָב מוֹכִיחַ. הָאִשָּׁה עַצְמָהּ מְבִיאָה אֶת גִּיטָּהּ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁהִיא צְרִיכָה לוֹמַר: ״בְּפָנַי נִכְתַּב וּבְפָנַי נֶחְתַּם״.
segments.en: The mishna explains: «What is» the difference «between a bill of divorce and death,» that certain women are deemed credible to testify about one but not the other? With regard to a bill of divorce, it is so «that the writing proves» that the husband is divorcing his wife, and the testimony is needed only to supplement the bill of divorce. Similarly, «the woman herself may bring her» own «bill of divorce, provided that she is required» by the court «to state» in its presence: «It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,» as the Gemara will explain.

moves.summary: Hostile relatives are credible to bring the get.
The woman may bring her own get with the declaration.

positions.claim: the hostile relatives may bring the get because the writing proves it; a woman may bring her own get if she declares it was written and signed before her
